actual.value: A pre-meeting on 5 March with key stakeholders from Myanmar media was held before lock-down from which important points and recommendations on mis- and disinformation were raised from the media representatives. A dialogue meeting was held online on 30 June 2020 with digital rights groups and civil society organisations.

target.value: 1)At the end of year 1, a communication plan has been developed.

title.narrative: Outcome: (1) Disinformation and hate speech are reduced, while reliable public-interest journalism reaches and engages audiences.

Number of stories incl. reach and engagement of stories produced during programme period. Number of posts/accounts removed on Facebook. Extend to which stakeholders participate and follow up on action plan.

target.value: 1) By the end of the project, at least one organization has been certified as factchecker and has been monitoring content since 1 April 2020. 2) By the end of the project, an identification model documents patterns of disinformers operates, and based on findings, content is produced and dialogue with Facebook is initiated. 3) Multi-stakeholder meetings have raised awareness on the issue of disinformation in Myanmar and key stakeholders are committed to an action plan. 4)Reliable and relevant content covering the election and disinformation has been published across the country.

title.narrative: Outcome (2): to find ways to ensure that the public continue to have access to relevant, reliable and inclusive public interest content by supporting independent media in Myanmar and outside of Myanmar, safeguarding media workers and catering to emerging needs of media institutions, network and associations.

target.value: 1) MJI to further develop and sustain a Myanmar-based framework for monitoring threats and attacks on journalists. 2) conducting research on gender specific safety issues with MJI, MWJS and other stakeholders. 3) The established safety hubs are in operation 4) development of safety guidelines and standard operational procedures for selected media outlets and media organisations 5) Safety trainings for female journalists and media workers

title.narrative: Hate speech and disinformation content creators are identified and content demoted and/or accounts removed.
Extend to which disinformation patterns are identified. Number of accounts/posts removed.

target.value: 5) By the end of the project, Frontier’s efforts to develop and apply a Myanmar version of Philippine Rappler is used for carrying out in-depth reporting on disinformers and it has been explored if it is feasible for use in other media houses.

actual.value: 5) Frontier that was inspired from the 'Shark-tank'-model by former Philippine IMS-partner Rappler – tracked and exposed online disinformation networks operating especially on Facebook. The coverage revealed several disinformation actors, which led to Facebook removing vast amounts of false and misleading content on the platform in addition to removing several accounts and pages spreading disinformation.

target.value: 1) At the end of year 1, the media house/organisation where the identification model will be institutionalised is selected and the collaboration with Rappler is initiated. 2a) At the end of year 2, information on disinformers is shared with Facebook to allow demoting of content and/or closing of accounts, depending on solid documentation. 2b) At the end of year 2, media house has produced and distributed journalistic stories under the topic of disinformation and coordinated inauthentic behaviour depending on solid documentation. 3) At the end of year 2, the implementing partner(s) has relevant safety procedures in place. 4) At the end of year 2, two meetings on verification tools have been conducted with participation of selected media houses.

actual.value: One organization has been selected and collaboration with Rappler has been initiated. Information on disinformers habe been shared with Facebook to allow demoting of content and closing accounts. Two media houses produced and distributed journalistic stories regarding disinformation. The selected organization has been using advanced verification tools.

title.narrative: Targeted media provide reliable and relevant election coverage reaching and engaging its audience in the election.
1) No. of stories covering the election produced and distributed by selected media. 2) Level of reach of produced content.

target.value: 4) At the end of the project, the selected media has continued their fact-checking and made it an integrated and sustainable part of their operation. 5) At the end of the project, the selected media are integrated into the Myanmar fact-checking community (linked to output 1).

actual.value:
During the entire programme period media houses have maintained reporting on disinformation and as a result all media partners have integrated this type of reporting to their daily news coverage.
Following the military coup on February 1, 2021, all independent media had their licences revoked and went into hiding or exile. Despite the many obstacles faced by media, all partners under this output have remained operational and returned to producing fact checking programme in a few months later.

target.value: 1) At the end of year 2, the selected media will have produced and distributed weekly election coverage over a period of 6 months. 2) At the end of year 2, the selected media have distributed election coverage nationwide measured trough engagement on Facebook and no. of audiences. 3) At the end of year 2, the implementing partners have relevant safety procedures in place.

actual.value: The two media partners produced programs and segments that debunked mis- and disinformation content which helped to educate audiences on media literacy. They produced similar TV programs debunking false information focusing on the COVID-19 pandemic and General Election which were published online and on TV. Misinformation Busters team produced 33 episodes over the course of the project consisting of 116 segments in 2020, with the top segment having over 500.000 views.

title.narrative: 2: Targeted media increasingly sustainable and trustworthy, producing public interest media content reflecting the diversity of society, and countering disinformation.

Output 2.1. Media, training institutions, networks and provincial media hubs strengthened in their ability to capacitate female and male journalists in public interest journalism and provide guidance for ethical standards. Output 2.2: Targeted media outlets including ethnic media, community media, networks of journalists and citizen journalists in Myanmar develop innovative approaches, have increased journalistic knowledge and competencies and are more resilient Output 2.3: Targeted media and CSOs counter disinformation and hate speech with content production, digital tools operating both inside and outside Myanmar.

target.value: 1) capacity building and training to safety hubs and local coordinators on Quick Response (QR) and monitoring 2) development of safety guidelines and standard operational procedures for selected media outlets and media organisations 3) establishment of the rapid response mechanism (protection fund) to support journalists’ and media outlets safety needs 4)specific support to female journalists based on identified needs

actual.value: •186 journalists (92 male and 94 female) from 37 different media houses have been trained - 80% of these journalists were based inside Myanmar and 20% were in exile. • Women in News Programme (WIN) was carried out jointly by WAN-IFRA and IMS-Fojo - 16 women journalists participated. • Supported female journalists: Group counselling sessions and stress management trainings (for 24 female journalists), as well as individual counselling (for 2 female journalists) who were released from prison and experienced trauma during the coup. • 15 story grants were handed out to women journalists in 2022, for the stories about the armed conflict; the post-coup displacement of women and children; as well as the lack of a justice system for sexual harassment and rape after the coup. • Core support to media houses inside Myanmar: 16 media houses were selected for support, which covered 7 states and 3 regions, for an immediate support to manage their

title.narrative: 3: Media stakeholders and CSOs are capacitated to promote laws and practices that protect and enhance freedom of expression and benefit from legal protection.

1: Capacity on media law and policy built for relevant stakeholders (CSOs, media associations). 2: The changes in media laws in Myanmar is continuously monitored and documented through ongoing legal analysis and international awareness raising 3: Media, CSO and journalists are provided with legal support and representation when needed.

target.value:
1) MJI organize safety trainings (online or physical) for all seven states and seven regions based on ToT, curricula and manual
2)Safety trainings for female journalists and media workers

actual.value: •Several online capacity building workshops were held in Myanmar with MyJustice network-based lawyers. •Series of in-person workshops (in Chiang Mai and Mae Sot) were held in 2022; focusing on international standards on freedom of expression in different areas and the role of journalists in documenting international crimes, etc. •Assisted media partners and journalists in engaging in solid human rights advocacy; and to report accurately on the legislative developments.

title.narrative: 1: Myanmar’s media actors are safeguarded and strengthened by gender responsive safety and protection measures.

Output 1.1: Attacks on journalists and other content producers and threats to their safety are continuously monitored and reported on (data sex disaggregated) Output 1.2: Safety and protection measures are made available to female and male content producers at national and provincial level in collaboration with local stakeholders. Output 1.3: Journalists and other content producers, women and men, safeguard themselves against legal, physical and digital threats.

target.value:
1) Myanmar Journalism Institute to further develop and sustain a Myanmar-based framework for monitoring threats and attacks on journalists. 2) MJI in cooperation with IMS-Fojo publish monitoring reports and disseminate these to key stakeholders and decision makers
3) research on gender specific safety issues with MJI, MWJS and other stakeholders

actual.value: • 8 senior journalists, located in highest risks areas were recruited and monitored physical, digital, and legal threats in their regions and provided information to MJI, and took part in bi-weekly meetings with IMS-Fojo. , 6 were relocated, including two in Mae Sot. 182 journalists, activists and some family members (150 men, 32 were women) •168 journalists (82 male, 86 female) from conflict affected areas participated in 15 safety trainings. • 5 media houses have finished their SOPs in 2022. •After the coup, the IMS-Fojo program took the lead in establishing a Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) program for Myanmar journalists, in collaboration with the Myanmar Journalists Network (MJN) and the Myanmar Women Journalists Society (MWJS). 25 individuals from these partner associations received training.

title.narrative: At least one certified third party fact checker in Myanmar established countering dis information and hate speech on Facebook.
A Myanmar organisation get certified factchecker via Poynter’s Institute and operate efficiently.

target.value: 1) At the end of year 1, mapping and selection of feasible fact-checking organisations has been conducted. 2) At the end of year 2, at least one organisation has been certified as factchecker and has been monitoring content since 1 April 2020. 3) At the end of year 2, the implementing partner(s) has relevant safety procedures in place.

actual.value: At least one certified third-party fact-checker in Myanmar through Poynter’s Institute established to counter disinformation and hate speech on Facebook

target.value: 4) By the end of the project, a fact-checking community has been established among fact-checkers and media in Myanmar. This will include transforming MIDO Advisory Board into a joint advisory board for the fact-checking community. 5) Throughout the extension period, fact-checkers continue to debunk false information, while building fact-checking capacity of other organisations, focusing especially on ethnic media outlets.
